note: When the input lacks a final newline, rendering appends one to the copied input buffer; for this candidate the final content line of three spaces becomes available to block parsing as a three-byte line before the appended newline.
The initial backtick fence is recognized at block level, so parse_fencedcode scans subsequent candidate lines looking for the closing fence.
The unterminated fenced block reaches the second line containing only three spaces; the line length passed to is_codefence is exactly 3 because the scan stops before the appended newline.
The indentation skipping permits i to become 3 for a line whose size is also 3; the missing safety obligation is that the index remain below size before it is used to read data[i].
With i equal to size, this reads one byte past the three-space line while trying to classify it as a code fence.
